> A custom ESP32-based PCB designed as a robotics controller for my Clunkey Rover project. The PCB will organize the rover's main electronics by providing connections for the ESP32, motor drivers, ultrasonic sensor, power system, and other peripherals. I want to design the schematic and PCB layout from scratch, learning how to turn my existing rover concept into a more organized and reusable electronics system. This project builds on my warm-up work while taking the electronics side of the rover further

ClunkeyCore — ESP32 Robotics Controller

Today I started my first week of work on ClunkeyCore, a custom ESP32-based robotics controller PCB. This project builds on my Clunkey Rover warm-up project, where I designed the rover chassis, planned the electronics, and created the firmware concept. Instead of making another rover, I want ClunkeyCore to take the electronics side of that project further by designing a real PCB.

I started by planning what the PCB needs to do and identifying the main parts of the system. The board is planned around an ESP32 microcontroller and will provide organized connections for motor control, sensors, power, and other robotics peripherals. I thought about how the PCB could make the wiring from my original Clunkey Rover design more organized and reusable.

I also worked through the initial project setup and learned more about what is expected for PCB Week. I chose to make ClunkeyCore a Tier 2 project because I want to go beyond a very basic development board and create something that is useful for a robotics application. I created the project repository and connected it to my Half Life project so that my development journal and bill of materials can be documented as I work.

My next step is to begin the actual schematic. I need to work out the electrical connections between the ESP32, motor-control circuitry, sensor connections, and power system before moving on to the PCB layout. I also want to make sure the design is organized and realistic before I start routing the board.

### 2026-10-07 – Yesterday I

**4h**

Yesterday I

![IMG_0104](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2DzupgroQiyESZ4TOplYYXhciyEobU0X/406fab8cfcd396484fecc229953d48546eb9baf74543e139b1abe680db161033.jpg)

![IMG_0105](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2DzupgroQiyESZ4TOplYYXhciyEobU0X/09ef2cf8dfb925f6eeaa65d69c6ebb56c4ee8e09e74f8f7a223debdb13ec4bd1.jpg)

started designing the ClunkeyCore PCB in Protoboard Designer. I set up the PCB workspace and grid, added the ESP32 footprint, and worked on finding suitable footprints for the other components. Since the exact TB6612FNG footprint was not available, I used a suitable pin-header-style footprint as a placeholder. I also placed the motor connectors, HC-SR04 connector, power input, and GPIO expansion around the ESP32 and began organizing the layout for cleaner routing.
What I learned:
I learned how to work with PCB footprints and arrange components based on their connections and physical layout. I also learned that choosing the correct footprint is important when designing a PCB.
